activities.caption: pair each box with what drawing it teaches
activities.name: mebBoxMatch

config.prompt: Choose the system boundary — pair each box with what it teaches you:

pairs.left: box around a reactor plus its recycle loop

pairs.right: what you are paying for at the fence line

config.why: The physics never changes — only the box. Learning where to draw it, and what to neglect once it is drawn, is the first genuine skill of the subject.

activities.anchor: Most design calculations assume steady state
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the master equation at work
activities.name: mebSteadyCloze

config.text: A process is at %%0%% when nothing changes with time: gauges read constant values, tank levels sit still, temperatures hold. Then accumulation is %%1%%, and the equation collapses to %%2%% equals %%3%% — like a shop whose daily takings exactly match its daily sales.
config.hint: The bathtub level sits still — what does that make the accumulation, and the two flows?

activities.anchor: concentrates fruit juice from 10 per cent solids to 50 per cent solids
activities.caption: call the product rate — the evaporator
activities.name: mebEvapEstimate

config.prompt: An evaporator concentrates juice from 10 per cent to 50 per cent solids, feed 1,000 kg per hour. Roughly what leaves as concentrated product?
config.why: 200 kg per hour of product — the solids balance reads 0.10 × 1,000 = 0.50 × P, and the total balance then hands over 800 kg per hour of vapour.
config.context: That vapour rate sizes the condenser and tells you the steam bill.

activities.anchor: steady state does not mean equilibrium
activities.caption: true or false — steady state versus equilibrium
activities.name: mebSteadyJudge

statements.s: A candle burning steadily is at steady state.
statements.why: Temperatures and flame shape are constant — but it is very far from chemical equilibrium.

statements.s: Steady state and chemical equilibrium are the same thing.
statements.why: Steady state is about flows balancing over time; equilibrium is about no net driving force left.

statements.s: Plants are engineered to run at states deliberately far from equilibrium.
statements.why: That is precisely where reactions and separations actually happen.

statements.s: At equilibrium a reaction has no net driving force left.
statements.why: Which is exactly why an equilibrium plant would produce nothing new.

activities.caption: file the bookkeeping — element or compound
activities.name: mebElementBuckets

config.prompt: In a reacting system, what is conserved and what changes identity? File each:
config.why: Atoms are never created or destroyed in an ordinary reaction — they only change partners; the compounds they form come and go.

activities.anchor: burning methane with 20 per cent excess air
activities.caption: call the oxygen feed
activities.name: mebOxygenEstimate

config.prompt: Burning 100 mol per hour of methane needs 200 mol per hour of oxygen. With 20 per cent excess for safety, how much oxygen is supplied?
config.why: 240 mol per hour of oxygen — arriving inside about 1,143 mol per hour of air, carrying 903 mol per hour of nitrogen that takes no part in the reaction.
config.context: The leftover 40 mol per hour is what the stack analyser reads as roughly 3.8 per cent oxygen.

activities.anchor: what a plant's oxygen analyser reads in the stack
activities.caption: drop the marker on the stack reading
activities.name: mebStackPlace

config.prompt: The dry flue gas from the complete burn reads near what oxygen percentage? Place the marker:
config.why: Near 3.8 per cent — 40 mol of leftover oxygen in about 1,043 mol of flue gas; operators read it to tell whether the burner is running rich, lean, or leaking air.

activities.anchor: The ammonia synthesis loop is the classic case
activities.caption: walk the recycle loop, in order
activities.name: mebLoopOrder

config.prompt: The ammonia loop, from feed to purge — put it in order:
items: Nitrogen and hydrogen enter the converter
Per-pass conversion is a modest 15 per cent
Ammonia is condensed out as product
Unreacted gas loops back to the converter
A purge bleeds out the inert argon at exactly the rate it enters
config.why: Per-pass conversion stays modest — which keeps the reaction controllable and the catalyst happy — while overall conversion of the fresh feed exceeds 97 per cent.
